theory.heading: Name the tool accurately
theory.body: Tool recognition begins with using the approved name rather than guessing from shape, colour or size. A tool may look similar to another item but have a different purpose, so visual appearance alone is not enough. In this course, examples include the disc sander and pedestal drill. Practical identification must match approved workshop images, labels and teacher guidance. Learning the correct name helps students understand instructions, discuss equipment clearly and avoid choosing an unsuitable tool. When uncertain, pause and ask for the approved name before making a decision.

theory.heading: Connect name and broad purpose
theory.body: Recognising a tool also means knowing its broad purpose without assuming how it should be operated. A disc sander is broadly associated with controlled abrasive material removal. A pedestal drill is broadly associated with producing holes using approved drilling equipment. These descriptions explain the general role of each tool, not a procedure for using it. The task information provided by the teacher determines whether a tool is suitable for a particular activity. A familiar tool name does not automatically give permission or enough information to begin practical work.

theory.heading: Use task information and approval
theory.body: Correct selection links three things: the approved tool name, its broad purpose and the specific task information provided by the teacher. Students should compare these before identifying a suitable tool. Approved images and current school SOP details control practical identification, while current SOPs and teacher directions control all actual workshop activity. If an image, label or instruction seems unclear, do not rely on memory, another student or a similar-looking machine. State what you recognise, identify what remains uncertain and wait for teacher confirmation.

questions.question: What is the best basis for naming a workshop tool?
choices: Its approved name shown through labels, images and teacher guidance
A nickname used by another student
The first similar tool found online
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Accurate recognition uses the approved name supported by workshop labels, images and teacher guidance.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Name the tool accurately and focus on what should be used instead of guessing from appearance.

questions.question: Why is visual appearance alone not enough to identify a tool?
choices: Every tool has the same shape
Similar-looking items may have different purposes
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Tools can appear similar while having different approved names and purposes.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Name the tool accurately and consider why shape, colour or size can be misleading.

questions.question: What should a student do when unsure of a tool name?
choices: Pause and ask for the approved name
Begin the task and identify it later
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Pausing and asking prevents inaccurate identification and unsuitable choices.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Name the tool accurately and find the recommended response to uncertainty.

questions.question: Which broad purpose is associated with a disc sander?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. A disc sander is broadly associated with controlled abrasive material removal.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Connect name and broad purpose and locate the general role linked to the disc sander.

questions.question: Which broad purpose is associated with a pedestal drill?
choices: Producing holes using approved drilling equipment
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. A pedestal drill is broadly associated with producing holes using approved drilling equipment.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Connect name and broad purpose and find the general role linked to the pedestal drill.

questions.question: Why do the broad purpose descriptions not give enough information to begin work?
choices: They replace the need for task information
They describe general roles rather than operating procedures or permission
They show that all tools can perform the same task
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Broad purpose explains a general role but does not provide operating instructions or permission.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Connect name and broad purpose and focus on the limit of a broad purpose description.

questions.question: What determines whether a recognised tool is suitable for a particular activity?
choices: The preference of the nearest student
The task information provided by the teacher
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Teacher-provided task information connects the tool and its broad purpose to the activity.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Connect name and broad purpose and identify what determines suitability for a task.

questions.question: Which three elements should be linked when selecting a suitable tool?
choices: Tool name, broad purpose and teacher-provided task information
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Suitable recognition connects the approved name, broad purpose and task information.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Use task information and approval and focus on the three linked elements.

questions.question: What controls practical identification of the disc sander and pedestal drill?
choices: The appearance of machines in other workshops
Approved images and current school SOP details
A guess based on their position
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Approved images and current school SOP details control practical identification.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Use task information and approval and locate what controls practical identification.

questions.question: What should a student do when an image, label or instruction is unclear?
choices: Select the tool that seems most useful
State the uncertainty and wait for teacher confirmation
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Identifying the uncertainty and waiting for confirmation prevents unsupported assumptions.
questions.retryFeedback: Review the final sentences of Use task information and approval and find the response to unclear information.

written.prompt: Explain how a student should identify whether a named workshop tool may suit a teacher-provided task without describing how to operate it.
written.sentenceStarter: The tool is called ___, and its broad purpose is ___. It may suit the task because ___, but the student must ___.
written.example: The tool is called a pedestal drill, and its broad purpose is producing holes using approved drilling equipment. It may suit a task involving a hole, but the student must check the approved identification and wait for teacher permission.
